title: Jenjen cucumber (Jenjen F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Jenjen cucumber is an F1 hybrid cucumber variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Jenjen cucumber is an F1 hybrid cucumber variety, also sold or known as Jenjen F1 or Ramgo Jenjen. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Jenjen cucumber is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Jenjen F1 or Ramgo Jenjen, this is the same cucumber. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cucumber variety finder](/crop-varieties/cucumber), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cucumber fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 42 to 45 days after sowing (Ramgo).
**Yield:** 55 t/ha potential (company figure), one Laguna grower picked every other day for about 45 days, some 22 harvests.
**Fruit:** Uniform, about 17 cm long and 4 cm across.
Fits as a relay crop between tomato or ampalaya plantings.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the cucumber growers in Majayjay and Liliw, Laguna, told Agriculture Monthly they plant any time of year for quick returns, with very few rejects. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Jenjen cucumber

Cucumber gives its first fruit fast, often in five to six weeks. Pick a variety bred to tolerate downy mildew if you plant near the rains. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Jenjen F1 the same as Jenjen?
items.a: Yes. Jenjen F1 is another name for Jenjen. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Jenjen?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
